claims.text: Mechanical-property variations across the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy family are governed by differences in local lattice distortion.
Mechanical-property variations across the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy family are governed by changes in stacking-fault energy.
Removing elements from equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni changes local lattice distortion and stacking-fault energy.
Local lattice distortion and stacking-fault-energy changes affect dislocation mobility.
Local lattice distortion and stacking-fault-energy changes affect transitions between deformation modes.
Changes in dislocation mobility and deformation mode alter alloy strength and ductility.
Differences in atomic radii among constituent elements produce different degrees of local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortion modifies stacking-fault energy.
Stacking-fault energy influences strain-hardening behavior and the balance between slip and twinning.
Reduced-constituent alloys will differ from the equiatomic quinary baseline in lattice distortion and stacking-fault energy.
Reduced-constituent alloys will differ from the quinary baseline in yield strength and strain-hardening rate.
Reduced-constituent alloys will show shifts in predominant deformation mode, such as earlier twinning or changed slip behavior.
Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni has a balanced lattice-distortion and stacking-fault-energy profile that produces its characteristic strength and ductility.
The proposed investigation is restricted to single-phase FCC alloys produced under comparable thermomechanical conditions.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when significant secondary-phase formation occurs.
Prior observations support a correlation between local lattice distortion and mechanical properties.
